Description: Controls feeding, growth, reproduction, recruitment, disease, predation, and survival.
Regulates metabolism, filtration, growth, spawning, and larval development.
Stable hard substrate supports larval attachment and reef persistence, whereas soft or rapidly accumulating sediments can bury or destabilize oysters.
Adequate oxygen supports respiration, feeding, and growth.
Water movement regulates salinity and transports larvae, oxygen, and food.
Depth influences exposure, temperature, oxygen conditions, and restoration feasibility.
High suspended-sediment loads can interfere with filtration and settlement. Sediment deposition can smoother oyster reefs.
Chlorophyll a is often used as a proxy for food availability.
